stem: What is the primary function of a 'skip to main content' link located at the top of a webpage?

options.text: To hide the repeated navigation links from screen reader users.
options.rationale: A skip link does not hide or remove content, the navigation stays available in the accessibility tree and can still be read.

options.text: To let keyboard users skip repeated navigation and reach the main content.
options.rationale: Skip links give keyboard and screen reader users a direct way past blocks of navigation that repeat on every page.

options.text: To reorder the page's tab sequence so the main content comes before the navigation.
options.rationale: The link moves focus when it is activated, it does not change the document order or the tab sequence that follows.

options.text: To return users to the top of a long page once they have finished reading it.
options.rationale: Returning to the top is the job of a back-to-top link. This link sits at the top and moves focus forward into the content.

explanation: Repetitive navigation headers at the top of every page force keyboard and screen reader users to press the Tab key dozens of times before reaching new content. A 'skip to main content' link satisfies WCAG Success Criterion 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks), under Guideline 2.4 Navigable, by moving focus past that repeated navigation.

references.title: WebAIM: Keyboard Accessibility - Skip Navigation Links
